The method operates on the existing AMR patch structure.
**Extended Patches:** Refined patches are logically extended to cover regions where dangling nodes exist, ensuring consistent value assignment.
**Pyramid Cells:** Coarse-level cells at the boundary to a finer level are decomposed into pyramids.
Each pyramid connects the coarse cell center to the vertices of a subdivided face facet.
This ensures that the scalar field is well-defined at all node locations required for marching cubes.
-   Identify the boundary faces of the coarse cell that touch the finer level.
-   For each such face, subdivide it into facets corresponding to the finer grid resolution.
-   Each pyramid connects the coarse cell center to the vertices of its corresponding facet.
Typical values depend on the specific dataset.
-   **Interpolation Method:** Used to assign values to dangling nodes.
-   **Dangling Nodes:** If dangling nodes are not properly assigned values consistent with the coarser level, cracks may still occur.
-   **Boundary Detection:** Correctly identifying coarse cells adjacent to finer levels is critical for proper pyramid decomposition.
The parent method that eliminates non-linear hanging nodes by subdividing boundary cells into pyramids.
Extended Patch Isosurface Extraction builds on this by preserving patch identity and extending patches for node-centered data [10502-cell-subdivision-isosurface-extraction.md].
The base algorithm used for isosurface extraction within the cells (including pyramids) created by this method.

Relies on consistent interpolation for dangling node values.
-   **When Not to Use:** When cell-centered data is used, or when patch identity is not required.
The method was developed to address the limitations of previous approaches that did not preserve cell identity or required complex handling of hanging nodes.
